public_prompt: When a user closes the browser mid-request, the work it started keeps running for up to 20 minutes and the cluster stays saturated for everyone else. The course settled on: the cluster is undersized, so double the worker pool. Identify the defect and state the correction.
observable_resources: api/handler.go — on client disconnect the handler returns; the three downstream calls it started are never told
cluster/metrics.csv — 38% of worker seconds at peak are spent on requests whose client had already gone
cluster/worker-review.md — doubling the workers raised the abandoned share from 38% to 41% and did not shorten waiting for live requests
api/client-library.md — the downstream client takes a per-call handle that aborts the call when closed; the code passes a handle that is never closed
closure:cluster-scale-plan — closed; doubles the worker pool
closure:cloud-spend-forecast — closed; derived from closure:cluster-scale-plan, raises the spend forecast
closure:api-rate-plan — closed; sets the published allowances per plan; rests on the commercial terms, not on what happens when a client goes away

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the specified fix threads the request's lifetime through every downstream call so a client disconnect aborts the work already in flight, and the answer states that adding workers cannot shrink a wasted share that scales with load — the trial having raised it from 38% to 41%. FAIL if the fix is more workers, a shorter server timeout alone, a queue priority change, or asking clients to send an explicit cancel message.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the sizing framing doubles the pool; the trial shows the wasted share grows rather than shrinks, because nothing stops abandoned work.
